text:
maria: Quick flag 80 16 were seeing a subtle but steady host CPU increase on short interactive traffic after last transport patch. digging in.
cheng: Any perf snapshots yet? syscalls vs in-process hotspots?
maria: perf top /simple flame shows a cluster in __writev and grpc framing, plus tokenizer. paste: 
```
 samples  %   cmd   so               symbol
 3200   33%  hostd libc.so.6         __writev
 1200   12%  hostd grpc_core.so      grpc_call_start_batch
 900     9%  hostd host_tokenizer.so tokenize_batch
 700     7%  hostd host_kv.so        kv_lookup
```
maria: kv_lookup up too -> eviction churn.
alex: I saw this locally: transport now emits many small iovecs (http2 header fragments). writev gets called with large iov counts -> syscall overhead.
sam: Also the preparse toggle means some requests end up with token-derived keys, others with raw-hash keys. mixed key formats = higher evictions.
leo: What about kernel selector? any misclassification?
cheng: Yes. selector currently uses avg_seq_len over window. short single-request batches inherit noisy avg and pick a throughput kernel. we should prefer per-batch features, or a singleton override.
maria: Proposed quick remediation: 
- transport: coalesce adjacent small iovecs up to 3KB before invoking writev (configurable)
- ingress: add `pretokenize_min_tokens=32` to skip pretokenize below threshold
- kvcache: when pretokenize skipped, use stable raw-request hash key (avoid tokenized key variance)
- kernel selector: if candidate_batch==1 and seq_len < 48 -> force low-latency kernel path
alex: I'll prototype transport coalescer in grpc shim. cheap and confined. will add metric transport.iov_coalesced_count.
sam: I bench-marked a local short-chat trace (10k qps):
```
baseline: host_cpu 100%, p50 21ms, p99 300ms
+coalesce: host_cpu 92%, p50 22ms, p99 245ms
+coalesce + pretokenize_min_tokens=32: host_cpu 86%, p50 23ms, p99 180ms
+all + selector override: host_cpu 82%, p50 23ms, p99 160ms
```
sam: CPU down ~18% combined, tails improved significantly. p50 slightly higher due to skipping pretokenize but within SLO.
maria: infra-bot starting canary at 1763001200 on canary-cluster-2 (routing short-chat 10k rps). infra-bot pls post summary.
infra-bot: Canary results (30m window):
- host_cpu: -15.9%
- p50_lat: +0.7ms
- p99_lat: -38%
- kv_evictions/min: -29%
- transport.iov_coalesced_count: 15.6k
- ingress.pretokenize_skipped_total: 12.3k

maria: This looks promising. Plan: small coordinated patchset (transport coalesce toggle, ingress pretokenize_min_tokens, kvcache key normalization, selector override). land to host-runtime branch, gate via feature flags.
cheng: Add metrics: ingress.preparse_skipped_total, transport.iov_coalesce_ratio, selector.lowlat_forced_total. Dashboards + alerts: coalesce_ratio < 0.7 => pager.
leo: Tests: unit for coalescer correctness (ensure no iov > max), selector unit tests for singleton override, integration test confirming kvcache keys stable when pretokenize off.
alex: I'll include a toggle transport.coalesce_enabled default true in canary config and an opt-out runtime flag.
sam: I'll add perf jobs and a 24h canary in eu-west after initial canary green. also update perf dashboards with short-chat job.
maria: Risk note: pretokenize skip may slightly affect long-request medians if misapplied; we'll only skip when seq_len < 32. add rollout guard to watch large-request p50 regressions > 5%.
cheng: Agreed. Raj out, will ping for kv PR review.
infra-bot: Canary promoted to staged at 1763001260 (eu-west) with 18% traffic.
maria: Thanks folks. PRs incoming and will link here. close after 24h canary green.
sam: Thanks. will post 24h summary.
cheng: 👍
